summary: Action log is a running list of everything an agent does during a task: each file it reads, search it makes, edit it saves and command it runs. Rows land one by one with a spinner, settle with a check and a time, and open to show their output, like a diff or test results.
use: When a coding or work agent runs many tool calls and people want a plain record of each one.
When people need to check the exact diff or command output behind a step.
When you want a header that says the agent is on step 4, then how many steps it took and how long.
features: Each action has an `icon`, a `title` (wrap file names in `<code>`), an optional `detail` line, and a `state` of running or done.
Running rows show a spinner. Done rows show a check and their `time`, like "0.4s".
Rows with `output` open on click to show it in a preformatted block. Lines wrapped in `dm-a` or `dm-x` spans read as added or removed.
While `running` is true, the header shows a spinner and "Running step N". After that it shows a green dot and "N steps, Xs", the total of the action times, unless you pass `status`.
`title` changes the header, which defaults to "Agent activity". It sits flat in a chat thread by default, and `bare={false}` gives it a card.
a11y: Rows with output are buttons with `aria-expanded`.
The actions are an ordered list (`<ol>`), so screen readers announce the step count and position.

faq.q: How do I add actions as the agent works?
faq.a: Append each new action to `actions` with `state: 'running'`, then set it to 'done' with a `time` when it finishes. Each new row plays a short entrance as it lands.

faq.q: How is the total time in the header worked out?
faq.a: It adds up the number at the start of each action's `time`, so write times in seconds, like "0.4s", for the total to make sense. Pass `status` to write your own line instead.

faq.q: Can I show a coloured diff in the output?
faq.a: Yes. `output` takes any React node, so wrap removed lines in `<span className="dm-x">` and added lines in `<span className="dm-a">`.
